description: Classifying a SERVICE response. The distinction that matters for funds is definitive-rejection versus ambiguous-outcome: a parsed {"status":"ERROR"} means the request was processed and refused, while a transport failure, an unparseable body, or a 200 that does not confirm means the mutation MAY have landed - and for rotate/split/merge the WALLET-generated secrets are then the only copy of the outputs, so they must ride the error rather than be discarded.

outcomes.pending: this k1 has another operation in flight (a melt); retry shortly
outcomes.spent: the SERVICE is authoritative that the note is already burned; a holder may lock it as spent
outcomes.unknown: the SERVICE does not recognise this note; surface it, do not silently lock it
outcomes.error: definitively rejected for some other stated reason
outcomes.ambiguous: the outcome is not known - preserve any fresh secrets

cases.name: melt success with a LUD-21 style proof
cases.why: OK on a melt means the payment is in flight, NOT that the note is confirmed spent

cases.name: pending
cases.why: the exact reason string LUD-25 specifies for a k1 mid-melt

cases.name: ambiguous callback wording is treated as spent
cases.why: an atomic multi-k1 callback cannot say which k1 failed; the spent reading is the safe one

body.reason: This mint is sunsetting - splits are disabled.

cases.name: 200 with neither OK nor ERROR
cases.why: the mutation was not confirmed and may still have landed
